mira: Quick RFC follow-up: propose we split routing into "penalty-generator" (pure, stateless) and "weight-assembler" (stateful, tenant-aware). Motivation: make policy logic composable and reduce churn in the runtime when we tweak penalties.

devon: Nice. How do you see the boundaries? e.g., does penalty-generator know about candidate health or just abstract signals?

mira: Proposal: penalty-generator consumes request context + candidate metadata snapshot (static descriptors only: region, tier, capacity class, model-compatibility flags). It must not call external stateful services. Health signals (live load, outage markers) stay in the weight-assembler or runtime so we don't violate determinism.

sam: That helps caching. If penalty-generator is deterministic given (tenant_tier, region_hint, prefix_hash, candidate_descriptor) we can memoize for short TTLs. Need a canonicalization rule for inputs. My suggestion: sort candidate list by route id before hashing, normalize region codes to lower-case, and drop ephemeral fields.

alex: What about rollouts and canaries? deterministic tie-breakers are critical, otherwise traffic oscillates. Perhaps include a stable per-tenant seed in the assembler so ordering ties break predictably.

mira: Agreed. We'll add a stable tie-break key: tenant_id + epoch_id (epoch only changes on deliberate policy updates). That way canaries are stable across small metric noise.

ops-bot: micro-sim results: small sandbox run (5k decisions) with splitter -> avg CPU per decision -4%, median selection latency -2.2%, event payload +1.2% due to penalty_vector. (job: route-mini-sim-2026-03-21)

devon: Config surface: limit plugin hooks to region_penalty, latency_penalty, cost_penalty and an optional custom_score hook. Each hook returns a numeric in [0,1]. We'll version the schema (v1) and require backward compatibility.

sam: Metrics: we should instrument penalty.gen.ms, assembler.ms, and also emit penalty.hash.v1 for cache hit debugging. Also a counter for deterministic-tie-breaks.used.

mira: Good names. Also need to think about fallback semantics: runtime keeps same behavior (try ordered candidates). But if assembler fails or returns malformed weights, runtime should have a compatibility flag to fall back to previous single-pass scorer. No hot path rollback in prod without the flag.

devon: Security note: penalty-generator must be safe to run in tenant sandbox (no access to secret keys). Keep input schema explicit and validate size (max candidates 32) to avoid amplification attacks.

alex: Ops/observability: add a small chart in routing dashboard: penalty-vector-size and penalty-gen-latency p95. For canary, we need per-tenant diff of ordering before/after so we can detect regressions in selection.

sam: Implementation notes: I'll prototype the serializer (compact binary) for penalty_vector to keep wire bytes down. If we keep fields fixed and small we can pack into 32 bytes per candidate.
mira: Action items: mira -> RFC PR with API example and canonicalization spec; devon -> schema draft + validation rules; sam -> prototype serializer + cache bench; alex -> canary dashboard template and stable tie-break generator. Target: land RFC and run a canary sim in staging next sprint.

alex: ack. I'll add the dashboard tickets.

mira: Thanks all. I'll @here when PR is up. :rocket:
